title: Loop Square
body:
Goal: draw a square with a for loop - 3 lines of code instead of 8.

  1. Open starter.py in Thonny and press Run (F5). The turtle goes in a straight line. Why? Nothing inside the loop turns it!
  2. Add t.left(90) inside the loop. Inside means: pushed in by 4 spaces, lined up exactly under t.forward(100).
  3. Press Run again.

Done looks like: a closed square, drawn by a loop that repeats 4 times.

Extra: change 4 and 90 to draw a triangle (3, 120) or a hexagon (6, 60). The secret rule: the turn is always 360 divided by the number of sides.

hints.label: Hint 1
hints.title: Where to look
hints.html: Run the program and watch the turtle. It goes in a straight line because nothing turns it. Find the # TODO comment inside the for loop in starter.py.

hints.label: Hint 2
hints.title: Try this
hints.html: Lines that are pushed in under the for line belong to the loop. Add a turning command there. It will run every time around the loop, right after the turtle moves forward. Line it up exactly under t.forward(100).

hints.label: Hint 3
hints.title: Almost there
hints.html: Under t.forward(100), type 4 spaces and then t.left(____). The blank is how many degrees a square turns at each corner. If you see an indent error in red, count the spaces on both lines and make them match.

starter.name: starter.py
starter.raw:
# Loop Square
# A for loop repeats the lines that are pushed in (indented) under it.

import turtle

t = turtle.Turtle()
t.shape("turtle")
t.color("#009E73")
t.pensize(3)

for i in range(4):
    t.forward(100)
    # TODO: add the turn here, lined up with the line above

turtle.done()
